description: §6.5.1 intercepted mutating methods keep their arguments verbatim: a string literal inside an object-literal argument to `@cell.splice(...)` / `@cell.push(...)` stays a string. #rep replaces row 1 with name "S"; #add appends a row named "tag". Was carried on impl#1 (S431, P7) as g-mutating-method-string-args-lose-their-quotes; closed by s461 (the argument list is lowered one ExprNode per argument).
rationale: §6.5.1: a mutating method called on a reactive cell performs that method's ordinary JavaScript mutation and notifies the cell's subscribers. Nothing in §6.5.1 rewrites the method's arguments, so `{ name: "S" }` is the string "S", never a reference to a binding named S. After #rep then #add the list is one→S, two, tag, the program compiles with no scope error, and the <each> shows three rows.
